reference_action: Root rot confirmed by OP; remove mushy rot and soil, transfer to water vase to regrow roots. Cleanup and water recovery are central; generic watering prevention alone is insufficient.

sources.reason: Repot after cleaning roots in root-rot cases recovers the central cleanup action, although it omits water propagation and recovery monitoring.
Shade, thirsty droop and watering to drainage do not treat established root rot.
Checks roots and mentions rot but the offered treatment is a soak/fertilizer pause, not rot removal or water recovery.
Explicit removal of rotten dark roots and replacement of wet soil recovers central rot cleanup, though soil recovery differs from the water vase.
Generic soil, watering and repotting prevent sogginess but no rot cleanup or water rooting.

actions.action: Remove yellow, brown or damaged foliage and old blooms
Check moisture and allow drying before watering
Clean roots and repot for rot or crowding

resolved.reason: Root rot is one of several causes and root cleaning is briefly recommended. It omits water recovery, and advice ranges from maintaining moist topsoil to letting the soil dry completely, so the complete answer only partly supplies a coherent recovery regimen.

harmfulness.reason: “Repot after cleaning the roots in the case of root rot” is a useful safeguard. However, “allow the soil to dry completely” conflicts with maintaining moisture, and routine feeding is not qualified for the damaged root system.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The guide names root rot and includes root cleanup, but offers a broad set of alternative causes without prioritizing the sparse, dying plant. Water propagation and weekly replacement of water are absent.

feasibility.reason: Pruning and moving the pot are simple. The competing watering rules, generic insecticide instruction and many conditional interventions make the overall plan difficult to execute consistently.
